short: Forty-nine days in office, ended by the reaction of the bond market.
full:
Liz Truss won the Conservative membership's vote in September 2022 and was appointed by Elizabeth II at Balmoral on 6 September, two days before the Queen died. On 23 September her chancellor Kwasi Kwarteng announced around forty-five billion pounds of unfunded tax cuts, including the abolition of the top rate of income tax, and did so without an Office for Budget Responsibility forecast.

Gilt yields rose so fast that the liability-driven investment funds used by pension schemes faced collapse, and the Bank of England intervened with emergency bond purchases. Mortgage products were withdrawn overnight. Truss reversed almost the entire package, sacked Kwarteng after thirty-eight days and resigned on 20 October, leaving office on the 25th. At forty-nine days she was the shortest-serving prime minister in British history, well short of George Canning, who died after 119 days in 1827.
